content: FileSensor's default 'poke' mode holds a full LocalExecutor worker slot for its entire wait duration (repeated blocking sleep(poke_interval) between checks) -- at scale, N dags waiting on file sensors exhausts worker slots even though the cluster is otherwise idle. 'reschedule' mode frees the slot between pokes but adds scheduler overhead and is recommended only for poke_interval >5 minutes (short intervals in reschedule mode can overload the scheduler). Deferrable mode (a custom Trigger) is the correct choice for file-wait: it offloads waiting to the triggerer's async event loop entirely, freeing the worker slot for the full wait duration regardless of interval length -- but see the separate trigger-blocking pitfall about keeping that async run() genuinely non-blocking (e.g. no sync os.path.exists loop without wrapping/backoff, no sync filesystem I/O directly in run() without executor offload).
